relevance_note: Family case report of LAMP2-related Danon disease: "Sanger sequencing confirmed that the proband, his mother, and his brother are carriers of this mutation".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no tables. Rows built with a short Python script from my own reading; spans checked verbatim by script. Labels use the pedigree labels printed in the Figure 2 legend (III‐1 proband, II‐2 mother, III‐2 younger brother, II‐1 father; U+2010 hyphen as printed). Father II‐1 is in scope as a tested-negative relative; he has no variant row. Disease label 'Danon disease' for II‐2 and III‐2 rests on 'we diagnosed the patients with Danon disease' (plural, not named) together with their carrier status; flagged as an inference. Proband's cardiomyopathy diagnosis 'At the age of 3 years' is recorded as onset of that feature, not as age at diagnosis of Danon disease (not stated). Variant type 'splice' from the title ('A family ... caused by a splice site mutation'); zygosity not stated for anyone, so not reported. Functional (RT-PCR) evidence recorded only for the proband, whose biopsy RNA was tested. Muscle biopsy, EMG and cardiac MRI findings (incl. 'delayed enhancement' in the Figure 1 legend, whose panels b,c the text ties to 'the patient') attributed to the proband. Normal findings handled per D-27: father 'normal electrocardiogram and echocardiography' and brother 'no obvious abnormality in the limb muscles' are whole-examination statements; recorded as written and they exclude no specific checklist item. Checklist judgments: proband 'intelligence is average' excludes intellectual disability (feature row) but the composite checklist item (also learning difficulties) left not reported; proband 'physical development was somewhat delayed' not mapped to the developmental-delay item (unclear whether growth or motor); mother 'slightly enlarged left ventricle' with normal systolic function and brother 'normal contractile activity' left not reported for the dilated/hypokinetic LV item; proband complete LBBB not counted as AV block; heart failure not stated explicitly. CK-MB and CK-MM values (no reference range) not recorded as abnormal. Contradiction in the paper: the abstract and results say the latter three of the six inserted bases form a stop codon, while another sentence says 'the second of which happened to be a stop codon'; this does not affect any recorded value.
